rounds.text: Karnavati Finance Ltd is displaying explosive top-line and bottom-line momentum that the market has yet to fully appreciate, evidenced by a staggering trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 527% and compounded profit growth of 134% [E17, E18]. This exceptional acceleration is highlighted by a massive year-over-year net profit surge of 1789%, indicating a profound turnaround that outpaces the broader sector median profit growth of 25.0% and sales growth of 16.8% [E45, E53, E54]. Crucially, a discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at Rs 2 per share against a market price of just Rs 1.35, offering a tangible margin of safety of 20.0% [E34, E35]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF implies that today's depressed price of Rs 1.35 only demands a modest 7.2% earnings growth, which is easily eclipsed by the company's current performance [E36]. Demonstrating strong internal confidence and alignment with shareholders, promoters have actively increased their stake to 62.06% as of June 2026, up from 58.64% in September 2023 [E32]. Conceded: [E28].

Despite robust headline sales growth [E17], Karnavati Finance Ltd suffers from catastrophic capital destruction and severe fundamental flaws that undermine its current valuation [E13]. The company generated a staggering negative return on equity of -81.0% in the latest period [E13], supported by a deteriorating 10-year median ROE of -5% [E23] and a low 3-year median ROE of -30% [E25]. This abysmal efficiency is mirrored in its ROCE of -4.4% [E12], significantly trailing the sector benchmark of 5.19% [E10]. Operational cash flows are equally alarming, with operating and free cash flows plunging to negative Rs -44.84 Cr in March 2026 [E28, E29]. Compounding these operational distress signals, the stock trades at an expensive price-to-book ratio of 3.14x against a book value of just ₹ 0.43 [E2], while offering a zero dividend yield [E4] and suffering a low interest coverage ratio [E41]. Furthermore, reported earnings are artificially propped up by non-core other income of Rs. 5.83 Cr [E43], and long-term shareholders have endured compounding share price declines of -13% over 3 years [E21] and -2% over 5 years [E20]. Conceded: the company displays rapid short-term sales and profit growth alongside an intrinsic value estimate above the current market price [E17, E18, E34].

The bear focuses heavily on historical ROE metrics [E13, E23, E25], but dismisses the explosive operational turnaround currently underway [E51]. Conceded: the company has a low interest coverage ratio [E41], negative operating cash flow for March 2026 [E28], and long-term share price declines [E21]. However, the market is anchoring to this stale sentiment while missing massive accelerating growth, evidenced by a 527% increase in trailing twelve-month sales and 134% profit growth [E17, E18, E51]. Furthermore, results score an impressive 81 out of 100 on the turnaround metrics, led by a staggering 1,789% year-on-year net profit surge [E45, E51]. The DCF intrinsic value of ₹ 2 per share provides a clear margin of safety above the current market price of ₹ 1.35 [E34, E35], and insiders are backing this up by increasing promoter holding by 3.42 percentage points to 62.06% [E32].

Conceded: promoters increased their holding by 3.42 percentage points to 62.06% [E32], and trailing twelve-month sales and profit grew by 527% and 134% respectively [E17, E18]. However, dismissing historical ROE metrics [E13, E23, E25] as stale ignores a catastrophic median return on equity of -81.0% last year and a 3-year median ROE of -30% [E25, E26]. While the bull cites an operational turnaround and an 81 out of 100 results score [E51], this surge is heavily polluted by ₹5.83 Cr of other income embedded in earnings [E43]. Furthermore, claiming the market anchors to stale sentiment while ignoring price action is contradicted by multi-year share price destruction, including a 13% drop over both 3 years and 1 year, and a meagre 1% growth over an entire decade [E19, E21, E22]. The touted margin of safety and DCF value [E34, E35] completely disconnect from reality when operating and free cash flows sit at a staggering negative ₹44.84 Cr for March 2026 [E28, E29]. Finally, this supposed growth engine is saddled with a low interest coverage ratio [E41], proving that explosive headline profit growth [E45] has translated into zero fundamental safety for shareholders.
